correctness.rationale: The quartic root formula is obtained exactly from 16v^4+(mu s^2-25)v^2-a(s)=0, with mu>400/9. Its uniform large-mu expansion gives the sharp area and thickness constants by an explicitly evaluated semicircular integral. The exact branchwise physical-time density retains the xy chemical prefactor; uniform comparison with integrable a(s)^(-1/2) proves the two period limits and weak phase occupation law. Along h=0 the cofactor equation gives the transverse multiplier, and the arclength gradient integral has a leading term 4sqrt(mu) integral(s sqrt(a)) and an O(mu^-1/2) remainder. Exact rational cofactor checks, numerical quadratures and large-parameter diagnostics were executed from the embedded standalone script verify.py; all finite tests passed, but analytical estimates, not finite numerics, prove the theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete relevant Theorem 3 and Lemma 13 of Craciun–Erban and the prior public quantitative note were inspected. The former states stable algebraic ovals and the cofactor; the latter gives exact period/multiplier quadratures and analyzes the opposite nodal-merger limit. Neither inspected text states or evaluates the mu-to-infinity lobe-area coefficient, axial thickness, rescaled time occupation, paired sharp period constants, or common growing Floquet action. The latter exact quadratures represent the closest stronger prior description and a genuine implication risk, but the present new limiting theorem needs a separate graph scaling with integrable endpoint asymptotics. Web and published-index searches found no exact equivalent. Lack of a match alone is not asserted to prove priority.

value.rationale: The four stable cycles and their parametric degenerations are natural dynamical objects in an explicit chemical oscillator. Large cross-coupling makes all four ovals thin, their actual physical periods vanish in two different proportions, and their shared transverse action grows rather than weakens; a rescaled physical-time phase law retains nontrivial nonuniform information. The area and multiplier constants have exact beta-integral values. This supplies motivated geometry and physical-time statistics rather than an arbitrary finite table or a cheap sign check.
